prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind O&M; scope to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere); excludes public grid, non-farm port ops. Wildmere: boundary/dispatch/status; Export Limit Advisory when capability<target; applies accepted ceiling, records time. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): validated commands within protections, blocks conflicts, safe mode on auxiliary loss; Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor feed Turbine Sensor Bus. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, export cable, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers, Fire Detection Panel; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; mode Substation Degraded. Substation Operator: approved switching, clearances, escalates alarms, notifies Grid Dispatcher; verifies equipment/switching points; accepts instructions only after state check and Control Engineer authorization; uses test trace to confirm restoration checks before next step. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-start on auxiliary loss, no unapproved paralleling, sheds loads; Start Test Trace. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): time-stamped data→Shore Control Room (Amber Quay); Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway. Shore Control Room: dispatch target/ramp, keeps last validated limit on grid comms loss; sends Switching Window Acknowledgment after period logged. Grid Dispatcher: targets, grid requirements/connection restrictions; priority safety>protection>export. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard): Position Quality Flag. Mode Grid Constraint: Duty Planner reassesses, gets revised authorization. Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): Squall Window Bulletin, Deferred Task Rationale, work period, dependencies. Weather Service→forecast→Weather Analyst (Wave Burst Record, Visibility Confidence Note) advises Duty Planner. Duty Planner: mobilization (CTV/Daughter Craft/SOV/Helideck), Transfer Manifest Addendum→Vessel Master; switching sequence with Control Engineer; records sequence/approvals/roles/final state/deviations/handover; authorizes restoration after Field Supervisor confirms personnel clear. Control Engineer: checks network, one-action-per-step instructions with hold points, verifies each reported state change. Operator reports each step completion. Ambiguity/comms failure/deviation: pause, safe state. CTV: Harness Audit Card. SOV: Recovery Basket Load Sheet. Storekeeper, Warehouse System: materials/cargo. Port Agent: Berth Slot Confirmation→Marine Coordinator (berths, vessel alignment, suspends access if unsafe). Mode Weather Hold. Vessel Master:

New part:
S538: An export restriction may arise from a grid instruction, a cable condition, or a substation operating limit.
S539: The Duty Planner treats a confirmed restriction as a Grid Constraint until the applicable limit is clarified or withdrawn.
S540: The SCADA Gateway presents current generation, export, and equipment status to the operations team.
S541: Grid Dispatcher receives the Export Limit Advisory and uses it to set the permitted export level.
S542: The Control Engineer verifies the permitted level, its effective time, and any required ramp rate before changing operating targets.
S543: The Fleet Dispatch Console supports coordinated adjustment of turbine output across the affected operating area.
S544: The Control Engineer reduces active power in controlled steps and checks that measured export follows the revised target.
S545: The Turbine Controller applies the accepted output target while retaining its protective control functions.
S546: The Pitch System adjusts blade angle within its operating envelope and does not override local protection limits.
S547: The Converter Cabinet remains within its electrical and thermal ratings throughout the reduction.
S548: The Export Cable Monitor is checked for temperature, loading, and alarm status during the response.
S549: The Offshore Substation operator confirms that export equipment remains within its approved operating range.
S550: The Main Transformer is monitored for loading and temperature, and any abnormal trend is escalated without delay.
S551: The Grid Interface Relay retains its protection settings unless an authorized switching plan requires a controlled change.
S552: The Control Engineer compares actual export with the permitted level and investigates any persistent mismatch.
S553: If the restriction changes, the Duty Planner records the revised operating basis and coordinates updated targets.
S554: The Maintenance Planning Engine is used to review whether the constraint affects planned work or equipment availability.
S555: Turbines are not repeatedly ramped to chase short-lived fluctuations that fall within the agreed control tolerance.
S556: The Nacelle Condition Monitor and turbine alarms are reviewed for signs that curtailment or ramping is stressing equipment.
S557: The Weather Service information is considered when weather conditions may affect operating margins or access decisions.
S558: The SCADA Engineer investigates telemetry gaps or inconsistent measurements before the team relies on them for control decisions.
S559: The Substation Operator reports any substation limitation that could require a lower export target or local equipment action.
S560: The Control Engineer escalates any condition that threatens equipment limits, protection coordination, or safe operation.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
